propositions: The decision_flips comprehension at parity.py:107 compares decision fields of gold pairs with no guard for errored=True, scoring a synthetic decision from an errored record as a model verdict flip.

An errored pair (valid=False, decision='dropped', errored=True) opposite a real verdict is counted as a decision flip, causing a single transient throttle to fail the parity gate as a quality regression.
A record with errored=True and valid=True produces a silent fabricated flip with no corroborating error-rate movement, undetectable in the reported metrics.

Three arms with 3 real flips, 2 real flips plus 1 error, and 0 real flips plus 3 errors all report byte-identical decision_flips=3 with no per-pair detail to distinguish genuine from fabricated flips.

Errored pairs are double-counted: once under criterion (b) as a decision flip and again under criterion (d) as error-rate regression, violating the parity.py:46 contract that errored is not a model verdict.
The gold-pair membership filter at parity.py:105 tests the label field, not decision; no out-of-vocabulary decision value can exclude an errored pair from flip scoring.
